analysis.file_name: GS Privorotsky - GS Basics Capex Concerns. Oil Debate. Texas. 3 Nov 2026.pdf
analysis.title: GS Basics: Capex Concerns. Oil Debate. Texas.
key_insights: Markets traded poorly on 2 Nov ahead of the US midterms. Tech could not hold despite a large pullback in energy. Gen AI fell 5%, AI healthcare 4%, optical 7.5% and neoclouds 6%, while homebuilders rose 4%, alternatives 3.5% and value 1.6%. High momentum fell 7%.

The author splits the move into two parts: a lack of support for the AI trade, with an early bounce fading into the US session, and a collapse in energy that pushed money into discretionary and retail. The result is a momentum unwind, with shorts rising and longs falling.

Apple's quarter beat but the outlook disappointed, and the stock fell about 3% after hours. December quarter gross margin guidance of 45-46% reflects higher memory costs, and services growth guidance of 8-9% was below expectations. AI demand supports memory pricing but competes for components and squeezes margins elsewhere.

Asia followed the US lower. The TSMC capex basket fell 8%, Asia AI bottlenecks 5.6% and Korea AI 5%, while airlines rose 2%. Japan was closed. TSMC in Taiwan broke its 100-day average and could test its 200-day.

Anxiety about AI capex is extremely high. Several bond issues launched on 2 Nov raise the question of the cost and availability of capital. Multiples have compressed sharply, with the SOX on a blended 24-month forward P/E of about 12.16x, approaching 2022 levels, and Nvidia at 10x, its lowest since 2013.

The author reads the multiple compression as the market pricing risk to estimates and possibly a 2027 peak in spending, because the cost of capital and the capacity to finance the buildout limit how fast companies can move. He draws parallels to the late 1990s, when capacity was built before there was enough use for it.

The author leans toward the bull case on AI. Robotics has barely started and enterprise IT workflow automation has barely scaled across legacy stacks. He also says corporate balance sheet capacity and debt market limits are real and binding.

AMD and Arista report on 3 Nov after the Intel and optical selloffs. AMD speaks to accelerator demand and competition, and Arista gives a read on hyperscaler networking spend. In this tape the reaction to guidance may matter as much as the guidance.

Energy fell about 8% on 2 Nov on headlines about possible US/Iran talks. Oil rose again after a Reuters report that the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island, which the author calls an odd fact pattern if talks were going smoothly. Middle Eastern equities outside Qatar did not rally and the Saudi ETF closed near its lows.

The author is nervous that the market got ahead of itself on oil and sees a risk of re-escalation after the midterms. Brent is bouncing modestly after the sell-off, and he calls the backdrop very unclear.

Positioning is defensive. Investors who made money in the first half are protecting gains, everyone is reducing risk without going far out the risk curve, and there was a lot of index-related hedging on Friday. Sentiment and positioning have come down meaningfully.

The S&P 500 has been higher 12 months after all 19 midterms since 1950, and gridlock has generally supported equities. AI and data center restrictions remain a risk. The author expects the clearing of events to be positive over time but says the AI trade needs stability first.

Sequence of hurdles named: avoid an extreme midterm outcome (Texas is the race to watch), then see whether the Middle East moves toward progress or re-escalation, then whether lower oil can deliver sustained relief in rates.

Risk of Middle East re-escalation after the US midterm elections.

tension_points.bull_case: Use cases are still largely untapped. Robotics has barely started and enterprise IT workflow automation has barely scaled across legacy stacks.
tension_points.bear_case: Cost of capital and capacity to finance the buildout constrain spending, 2027 could be a peak, and bond issues raise questions about the availability of capital. Multiples have compressed to 12.16x for the SOX and 10x for Nvidia.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Corporate balance sheet capacity and debt market limits, which the report says are real and binding, constraining how quickly companies can build.

tension_points.bull_case: Headlines point to possible US/Iran talks, which drove an 8% energy drop, and lower oil could deliver sustained relief in rates.
tension_points.bear_case: Oil rose after a report of a US strike on Qeshm Island, Middle Eastern equities outside Qatar did not rally, the Saudi ETF closed near its lows, and the market may have gotten ahead of itself.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A move toward re-escalation rather than progress in the Middle East after the midterms.
